paragraphs.text: Contraption is an artifact type that appears on nontraditional cards from Unstable . Contraptions have a unique card back and start the game in a separate deck. The assemble keyword action lets a player put the top card of their Contraption deck face up onto the battlefield on one of three sprockets. During each player's upkeep , if they control a Contraption, they advance to a new sprocket and crank any number of that sprocket's Contraptions, triggering those Contraption's abilities. Sprockets are moved through sequentially, tracked with the CRANK! counter : Sprocket 1, 2, then 3, then back to 1. Therefore, each Contraption can be cranked once every three turns. A player chooses the order in which Contraptions are cranked each time they move the CRANK! counter, and cranking a Contraption is optional.

The term "assemble a Contraption" first appeared on Steamflogger Boss ( Future Sight ) as a joke; it wasn't defined until Unstable , which also introduced Contraption cards. Although the Comprehensive Rules lists the Contraption artifact type and the assemble keyword, it does not define these terms beyond pointing to the Unstable FAQ. The functionality of Contraptions is therefore confined to silver-bordered rules.
Contraptions represent machines or devices that appear strange or unnecessarily complicated, and are often badly made or unsafe.

The Contraption deck is the collection of Contraption cards that a player plays with. It is a subset of the command zone . Like a normal deck , it is shuffled and placed face down at the start of the game. Players don't lose the game for attempting to assemble from an empty Contraption deck.

In Constructed formats, a Contraption deck must have at least fifteen cards and may not have more than one copy of the same card; in Commander specifically, Contraptions do not count as a part of the 100-card deck, and color identity does not exclude any Contraptions from the deck. In Limited formats, a player may include any combination of Contraptions they open or draft , and may include duplicates.

Contraptions may be assembled by players or creatures ( Riggers ). There is no functional difference between the two. However, Steamflogger Boss only cares about Contraptions assembled by Rigger creatures.

Once assembled, Contraptions are permanents on the battlefield . They can be destroyed and otherwise interacted with like any other artifact . However, if a Contraption would leave the battlefield and go to any zone except exile , it's instead put into the scrapyard , a special zone for broken Contraptions. Contraptions that enter the battlefield without being assembled are immediately put into the scrapyard.
One card, Clock of DOOOOOOOOOOOOM! , allows a player to advance their CRANK! counter and crank their Contraptions outside the normal window.

Suspicious Nanny and Cogmentor use the keyword reassemble, which means to move a Contraption to any one of your sprockets. When a player reassembles an opponent's Contraption, they also gain control of it.

The term "assemble a Contraption" first appeared on the card Steamflogger Boss ( Future Sight ). It was meant as a joke; the senior director of R&D wrote that there no intention of ever turning it into a real mechanic. Following this statement, Head Designer Mark Rosewater received frequent requests for Contraptions to become real. Eventually, Rosewater vowed to fulfill this request before he retired.

Kaladesh seemingly fitted the right circumstances for contraptions, but Rosewater argued against it. Contraptions were finally introduced in Unstable , as revealed by Mark Rosewater at SDCC 2017 . The design of Unstable predated Kaladesh .

Contraptions have a watermark placed in the bottom right-hand corner to show which Unstable faction they belong to. They are borderless , so they could potentially be used with Eternal-legal cards one day. However, because of the different card back , they are currently not Legacy legal .

Steamflogger of the Month Creature — Goblin Rigger When this creature enters, it assembles a Contraption for each Contraption you control. (To assemble a Contraption, put the top card of your Contraption deck face up onto one of your sprockets.) 3/3
